guidance.heading: Full-year 2026 Guidance
section: Our Payments TPV and Fintech average balance sheet growth guidance remains on track and unchanged.
Marketplace GMV growth is now expected to be around 12% year-over-year.
Even with softer GMV trends, lower Fintech funding costs mean we are able to once again reiterate our guidance of around 5% Kaspi.kz consolidated adjusted EBITDA growth year-over-year in 2026.
Our guidance assumes constant-currency exchange rates as of January 1, 2026.

desk.headline: Revenue up 18% in constant currency to KZT1.1tn but adjusted EBITDA only +1%; Marketplace GMV guidance cut to ~12%, EBITDA growth target of ~5% kept

other.label: Revenue
other.change: +18% y/y constant currency, about flat reported

results: Revenue grew 18% in constant currency to KZT1.1tn, but was roughly flat as reported because the Turkish lira fell 32% against the tenge.
Profit growth stalled: adjusted EBITDA rose 1% to KZT408bn and net income was stable at KZT281bn, held back by higher deposit costs and spending at Hepsiburada in Türkiye.
Marketplace revenue rose 20% (constant currency) on higher take rates, advertising and delivery, while GMV grew only 8% as a strong tenge pushed average selling prices down 8%.
Fintech revenue grew 19% to KZT489bn, but its EBITDA slipped 1% as funding costs rose to 14.9%; cost of risk was steady at 0.6%.
Board proposed another KZT1,000 per ADS quarterly dividend; plans to grow Magnum Daily convenience stores from a 42-store pilot to about 300 by end-2027.

guidance.summary: Kaspi cut its 2026 Marketplace GMV growth guidance to around 12% (constant currency) because of lower prices per item in Kazakhstan, but reiterated about 5% growth in consolidated adjusted EBITDA as lower funding costs offset the softer GMV. Payments TPV and Fintech balance-sheet guidance is unchanged.

items.metric: Payments TPV and Fintech average balance sheet growth

points: CEO letter: consumers are buying more often, with yearly e-Commerce purchases per consumer up 27%, even as a stronger tenge lowers prices.
Two 100bp cuts to the 3-month deposit rate (August and October) should ease funding costs from Q4, with a bigger profit benefit in 2027.
Spending in Türkiye is expected to moderate significantly in 2027; the Hepsicredit shopping loan already funds about 8% of smartphone GMV there.
Magnum Daily pilot stores reached about 15% store-level EBITDA margin; medium-term ambition is roughly 3,000 stores.
The Kasper AI shopping assistant has 1.4m users, with conversion 1.5 times that of text search.
